decisions.reason: The address autocomplete web service builds directly on the firm's established address and market-data databases, so its in-house R&D and data expertise let it interpret results and keep refining the service.
The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's core grid-fee data know-how to a neighbouring market, which it can assimilate well, though demand in that foreign niche is less certain.
Peak load window determination is a regulated network-operator calculation close to the firm's core analytics, so it fits the platform strategy and the firm can improve it with its own R&D.
The end-customer tariff database is a multi-model line close to the firm's long-built industry databases, giving it strong related knowledge and fitting the move toward SaaS and data services.
Custom web services draw on the firm's software development and internal data center and support its end-to-end service model, although bespoke offers could be folded into the broader platform.
The postal code lookup service builds on established address and grid-area data the firm already maintains, so it is cheap to sustain and easy to improve.
